items.title: Building AI So Everyone Can Flourish
items.summary: A large language model knows everything and nothing at the same time. Tim O’Reilly , founder and CEO of O’Reilly Media , joins us ahead of his keynote at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America to talk about what that paradox means for the people building with these models. We start with what Tim is bringing to the stage in San Jose, then move to the craft of steering a model. The right words work almost like spells that open up new regions of latent space. Something as small as telling a model to use a computer can unlock a new tier of capability, where agents go off and do real work. From there, the conversation turns philosophical. Tim makes the case for mechanism design: shaping the rules of a system so the outcomes we want become the natural ones. We connect it to a book, The Score, and the question of which game we are really playing. In Risk, everyone fights over the board. In charades, everyone plays together. We close on Tim’s view that AI should be an ecosystem rather than a product that sucks the air out of the room, so that everyone can build on top of it and flourish. We start with what Tim is bringing to the stage in San Jose, then move to the craft of steering a model. The right words work almost like spells that open up new regions of latent space. Something as small as telling a model to use a computer can unlock a new tier of capability, where agents go off and do real work.


From there, the conversation turns philosophical. Tim makes the case for mechanism design: shaping the rules of a system so the outcomes we want become the natural ones. We connect it to a book, The Score, and the question of which game we are really playing. In Risk, everyone fights over the board. In charades, everyone plays together. We close on Tim’s view that AI should be an ecosystem rather than a product that sucks the air out of the room, so that everyone can build on top of it and flourish.

items.title: Alastair Graham: FOSS4G:UK 2026
items.summary: This episode is a quick conference update from FOSS4G:UK 2026 in Leeds by Alastair Graham, covering what happened across the two days and why it mattered. Al highlights the attendance, sponsors, community atmosphere and the strongest themes running through the programme. The focus is on the talks and sessions he attended, from artificial intelligence and geospatial workflows to cloud native elevation data, QGIS management in a large enterprise, drones, and humanitarian mapping. Al also reflects on what worked well in the event format and what might be tweaked for future conferences. Videos of the sessions will be online as soon as possible. Show notes on the Geomob website , where you can also learn more about Geomob events and sign up for our monthly newsletter.

items.title: Rethinking Accountability for AI-Generated Work - with Chris B Kennedy of Regions Bank
items.summary: As AI quietly drafts more of the reports, pitch books, and client materials leaving financial institutions, few firms have settled who is accountable for what it produces. In this episode, Chris B. Kennedy, Managing Director of Strategic Technology & AI at Regions Bank, examines why ownership of AI-generated work splits into legal, regulatory, and human-accountability questions that most AI policies don't yet answer. He walks through why percentage-based AI usage rules fall short, why AI detection tools can't be trusted for high-stakes decisions, and what it takes for a leader to stand behind work AI helped create.
